nodes.label: 62-year-old male patient had cough, sputum, and intermittent fever for 3 days
Patient is a 62-year-old male waste disposal worker with recent poor sleep of 2-3 hours per day

Past medical history: tuberculosis 10 years ago, cured after systematic anti-tuberculosis treatment; no history of diabetes mellitus, malignant tumors, organ transplantation, or long-term use of glucocorticoids or immunosuppressive drugs
Before admission, highest temperature reached 41°C with chills, cough, and yellow sputum; no abdominal pain, diarrhea, or joint pain
Physical examination on admission: temperature 40.2°C, other vital signs normal; few wet rales audible on lung auscultation
Chest imaging shows bilateral patchy and nodular high-density shadows with consolidation
Laboratory tests show elevated white blood cells, neutrophils, CRP, and ESR
Respiratory pathogen nucleic acid test result is negative
No confirmed specific zoonotic exposure event is documented; only occupational risk as a waste disposal worker
Sputum culture and pneumococcal antigen test results are not yet available
No preceding influenza-like illness or healthcare-associated exposure is documented
No underlying chronic lung disease is documented
